---
title: "R and Python chunks with timeknit"
format: html
engine: knitr
---

A knitr document can mix R and Python chunks; reticulate runs the Python
chunks and shares objects between the two languages. timeknit times every
chunk the same way regardless of its engine. Render this file with
`quarto render mixed-reticulate.qmd` or `rmarkdown::render()` after activating
timeknit (see `?use_timeknit`).

```{r}
#| label: r-data
library(reticulate)
x = rnorm(1e5)
```

The first Python chunk also pays for starting the interpreter and importing
modules, so it is often the slowest chunk in the document.

```{python}
#| label: py-import
import numpy as np
import time
```

```{python}
#| label: py-compute
arr = np.array(r.x)
time.sleep(0.5)
summary = {"mean": arr.mean(), "sd": arr.std()}
```

```{r}
#| label: r-back
str(py$summary)
```

```{python}
print("an unnamed python chunk")
```
